summary: Feed s119_double to NDR is degraded: 2.3% TCP packet drops and 29.2% ERSPAN-encapsulated traffic. Drops break flow reassembly and tunnel encapsulation blinds NDR to inner payload for nearly a third of frames.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is dropping packets upstream of the NDR (34 of 1493 TCP packets, 2.28% > 1% threshold). Tool overload check is healthy, so drops are not at the NDR NIC but in the visibility fabric - typically ingress oversubscription, buffer exhaustion, or SPAN/broker policing causing random gaps across flows.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires both directions and full payload for flow reassembly and detection. Missing segments cause incomplete TCP streams, failed reassembly, missed signatures/anomalies, and increased false negatives. Retransmits and gaps also waste NDR processing.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute load across NDR cluster or add packet broker load-balancing to eliminate broker-level drops and keep per-tool rate below 10 Gbps port capacity while preserving flow coherence.

findings.root_cause: 29.2% of frames (453 of 1554) arrive encapsulated in ERSPAN and are delivered still-encapsulated to the tool. Packet broker is forwarding ERSPAN from remote TAP/SPAN without stripping the tunnel header.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR sees outer ERSPAN/IP/GRE headers instead of inner customer L2-L7. Without ERSPAN decapsulation the NDR cannot parse inner flows, extract payload, or apply detections - creating a 29% blind spot despite needing full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to terminate/strip ERSPAN and forward only inner original frames so NDR receives decapsulated, parsable traffic for full detection coverage.
